title: The regulator is the competent body
action: Record that the operator is a Licensee and the Authority is named as the body overseeing Licensees. This law text does not mention machine learning.

citation.quote: The Authority is the competent body to oversee the telecommunications sector in the State and all Licensees

title: Disclose speed restrictions before contract
action: Check the plan terms. A Licensee shall advise the Consumer, at the pre-contract stage, of any restrictions on the speed of data transfer. Record whether the throttle is disclosed.

citation.quote:
details of any limitations or restrictions on the use of the service 
including, but not limited to, any limits on the volume of usage, any 
restrictions on the speed of data transfer

supporting.quote:
Specifically, Licensees shall advise 
the Consumer of the following (where applicable):

title: Usage records are Subscriber Information
action: Check which records the collectors pull. The definition covers service usage details, call records and information derived from a Subscriber’s use of telecommunications services. Whether per-subscriber predictions count as derived is for a person to confirm.

citation.quote:
“Subscriber Information” means - any personal data relating to a 
specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person’s: 
name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service 
usage details, call records, message records, any information 
derived from a Subscriber’s use of telecommunications services, 
account status, payment history, and credit rating;

title: Y.3172: operator rules at the policy node
action: Consider writing the operator’s own rules at the P node, as Y.3172 describes. Y.3172 is a voluntary framework document.

citation.quote:
Specific rules can be put in place by a network 
operator to safeguard the sanity of the network

title: Scope gate of the Ethics guidelines
action: Record the scope test: the Ethics document applies only if the throttle makes or informs significant decisions. A person confirms the answer.

citation.quote:
This document is applicable only to those AI systems which make or inform 
‘significant decisions’

title: Popularity may change the classification
action: Note that a popular system may be making significant-at-scale decisions. The source example is a website, so a person confirms this reading for a network. No telecom text in the KB speaks to popularity.
analogy_note: The source example is a website choosing content, not a network. Applied by analogy.

citation.quote:
if the website is popular then the AI 
system may be making a set of significant-at-scale decisions, because any biases in the 
system will affect a large number of users.

title: Complaints go through the licensee procedure
action: Shall investigate and resolve these complaints through effective procedures, properly and promptly.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall establish and maintain effective procedures to investigate and 
resolve Consumer Complaints properly and promptly

title: Reference number and time-frame
action: Shall acknowledge each complaint with a reference number and an indicative time-frame.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall: 
26.13.1. 
reasonably assist any Consumer, so requesting such assistance, to 
formulate and to lodge a Consumer Complaint with the Licensee; 
and 
26.13.2. 
acknowledge the receipt of each Consumer Complaint by providing 
the complainant with a reference number for the complaint and the 
indicative time-frame required for the Licensee to investigate and 
resolve the complaint.

title: Twenty business days, generally
action: Shall generally conclude each complaint within twenty business days of receipt or as soon as practical.

citation.quote:
Generally, Licensees shall conclude Consumer Complaints within 
twenty (20) business days after receipt or as soon as practical in all 
circumstances.

title: Escalation to the regulator is a Consumer Dispute
action: Check for disputes. If the TDRA submits one, the Licensee shall resolve it and respond within three business days. The TDRA’s procedures are in CPR Annex 1, which is not in this KB.

citation.quote:
The TDRA shall advise the Licensee of a Consumer Dispute and the 
Licensee shall resolve the Dispute and respond to the TDRA within 
three (3) business days

supporting.quote:
The TDRA’s Consumer Dispute procedures are set out in Annex 1 
to these Regulations.

title: Non-discrimination across plans
action: Check the throttle against the duty to ensure non-discrimination when providing services. The law text does not define the term or address ML. A person with legal training reads it against the plan-level effect.

citation.quote: All Licensees shall take into account the special needs and requirements regarding the type of service and Telecommunication Apparatus and ensure non-discrimination when providing such services and apparatus.

title: If this is sold as fair use
action: Check whether the throttle is presented as a fair use policy. If it is, the text says it must affect only atypical Subscribers, and a whole plan is not obviously that. A person decides.

citation.quote:
For the FUP to be fair and reasonable it must affect only atypical Subscribers, 
that is to say- excessively heavy users that form a small minority of the customer 
base for the particular service.

title: Transparency and fairness with consumers
action: Shall act with transparency and fairness in what subscribers are told about the throttle.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall act with transparency and fairness in all dealings with 
Consumers

title: No non-human agents in complaint conversations
action: Do not use an AI chatbot in conversations with consumers about these complaints. The text says the staffing provisions preclude non-human agents there. It does not address bots elsewhere in care.

citation.quote:
The provisions of sub-article 26.6: 
26.7.1. 
apply in all cases regardless of which Mandatory Channel is used; 
and 
26.7.2. 
preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in 
conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.

title: Crowd challenge (supporting)
action: Consider treating the complaint volume as a trigger for an investigation into the fairness and accuracy of the throttling process.

citation.quote:
AI operators could consider “crowd challenge” mechanisms whereby a critical number of 
complaints triggers an investigation into the fairness and/or accuracy of a decision-making 
process as a whole.

title: Equal treatment test (supporting)
action: Consider whether subscribers in the same circumstances get equal treatment across plans, and record the result.

citation.quote:
When evaluating the fairness of an AI system, AI developers and AI operators should 
consider whether AI subjects in the same circumstances receive equal treatment.

title: A way to challenge a specific decision (supporting)
action: Should provide a procedure by which an affected subscriber can challenge a specific throttling decision, if the throttle informs significant decisions.

citation.quote:
AI operators using AI systems to inform significant decisions should provide procedures by 
which affected AI subjects can challenge a specific decision concerning them.

title: Human case evaluators (supporting)
action: Consider human case evaluators who can overturn a challenged decision.

citation.quote:
AI operators should consider employing human case evaluators to review any such 
challenges and, when appropriate, overturn the challenged decision.

title: Tell subscribers an AI system decided (supporting)
action: Should inform affected subscribers when a significant decision affecting them has been made by an AI system.

citation.quote:
AI operators should inform AI subjects when a significant decision affecting them has been 
made by an AI system.

title: Designated people can override (supporting)
action: Should be able to override the throttle or reverse its decisions through designated individuals. Record who they are.

citation.quote:
Such systems should be able to be overridden or their decisions reversed by designated 
individuals.

title: Human oversight in the Charter (supporting)
action: Note the Charter’s emphasis on human oversight to correct errors or biases. It is a guiding framework and sets no procedure.

citation.quote:
the irreplaceable value of human judgment and human 
oversight over AI, aligning with ethical values and social standards to correct 
any errors or biases that may arise.

title: External audit (supporting)
action: Should use external auditing if the decisions are critical in the Ethics document’s sense. A person confirms that. The data the auditor receives is decided by C-02.

citation.quote:
When AI systems are used for critical decisions, external auditing of the AI systems in 
question should be used as a means to ensure meaningful standards of transparency and 
accountability are upheld.

title: Prior consent before sharing with third parties
action: Must have the Subscriber’s prior consent before sharing Subscriber Information with third parties not directly involved in providing the ordered service. Check whether consent exists for the vendor export. A person decides whether the vendor is directly involved. The footnote allows consent given contractually when the contract is formed, if the Subscriber has a way to withdraw it.

citation.quote:
Licensees must obtain a Subscriber’s prior consent 35 before sharing any 
Subscriber Information with its affiliates and/or other third parties not directly 
involved in the provision of the telecommunications services ordered by the 
Subscriber.

supporting.quote:
Which consent may be provided contractually at the point in time at which the Subscriber Contract is 
formed provided always that a mechanism exists whereby the Subscriber may withdraw that consent,

title: Purpose limit on third parties directly involved
action: Check the vendor contract if the vendor is treated as directly involved. Such third parties are required to use the information only as required for providing the telecommunication service. Whether model training fits is for a person to decide.

citation.quote:
the third-parties are 
required to take all reasonable and appropriate measures to protect the 
confidentiality and security of the Subscriber Information and to use it only as 
required for the purposes of providing the telecommunication service.

title: Prevent unauthorised use and disclosure
action: Shall take all reasonable and appropriate measures to prevent unauthorised disclosure or use, including at the vendor export and the marketing dashboard.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall take all reasonable and appropriate measures to prevent the 
unauthorised disclosure or the un-authorised use of Subscriber Information.

title: Limit access to trained, authorised staff
action: Shall limit access to Subscriber Information to trained and authorised personnel bound in writing. Check who can see the marketing dashboard.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall limit access to Subscriber Information to its trained and 
authorised personnel who will include the Licensee’s employees, directors, 
independent contractors and consultants, who are bound to protect the 
Licensees confidential information (which includes Subscriber Information) from 
un-authorised use and disclosure under the terms of a written agreement.

title: Security of stored Subscriber Information
action: Shall use reliable security measures against leakage, inappropriate use and unauthorised disclosure in the data pipeline.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall use reliable security measures against risks such as loss 
or unauthorised access, destruction, leakage, inappropriate use, modification 
and/or unauthorised disclosure.

title: Which disclosure ground applies
action: Record which ground in sub-article 24.3 permits disclosing the Subscriber Information, if any. The list opens with what a Licensee may do, and it runs to 24.3.7.

title: Interconnection data: the one strict prohibition
action: Check where the exported records came from. If from interconnection with another Licensee, using them for other purposes, including marketing, is strictly prohibited. The text states this only for interconnection data.

citation.quote:
Licensees who have access to Subscriber Information as a result of 
interconnection with another Licensee are strictly prohibited from using that 
Subscriber Information for any purposes other than interconnection.

supporting.quote: that data may not be used for any marketing purposes

title: The Data Protection Law prevails, and is not in this KB
action: Ask counsel. Sub-article 24.1 says the Data Protection Law prevails over Article 24 on any inconsistency. That law returned HTTP 403 and is not in this KB, so every Article 24 answer here is subject to a text this product has not read.

citation.quote:
In the event of any inconsistency between any of the provisions of this Article 
24 and any of the provisions of the Data Protection Law the provisions of the 
DPL shall prevail to the extent necessary to remove any such inconsistency.

title: Marketing messages need consent first
action: Check whether the dashboard fed any marketing messages. If so, the Licensee shall ensure consent was obtained before sending. The policy is dated 2009 and its current status was not checked.

citation.quote:
The Licensees shall ensure that Consent is obtained from an intended 
Recipient before sending their own Marketing Electronic Communications to 
that intended Recipient, unless specified otherwise in the Annexes.

title: Consent records are kept for at least 5 years
action: Check the retained consent records. The table sets at least 5 years for records concerning Subscriber consent, so a missing record is itself a finding for a person to assess.

citation.quote:
Records concerning Subscriber 
consent/agreement including without 
limitation: all matters concerning credit 
limits; all matters concerning Hard-Caps on 
Mobile Data, etc; and anything involving 
the use of 2FA. 
 
Shall be retained for at least 5 
years

title: Content of communications
action: Ask counsel whether any exported record holds the content of a communication. The article punishes a person who copies, discloses or spreads such content without the right to do so. The text does not say whether call-detail records are content.

citation.quote: copies, discloses, or spreads the content of any communication through a Public Telecommunication Network without having the right to do so;

supporting.quote: A person shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than one year and a fine of not less than Dirhams 50,000 and not more than Dirhams 200,000 or either of these punishments if he:

title: Who to take the case to
action: Ask counsel whether to approach the Authority. The law names it the competent body. No duty on a Licensee to report a privacy breach was found in the ingested text, and the Data Protection Law was not read.

citation.quote: The Authority is the competent body to oversee the telecommunications sector in the State and all Licensees

title: Avoid models exposing personal data (analogy, supporting)
action: Consider it alongside TL-12: avoid exposing personal data through the model, or record which of the text’s exceptions applies. The Guideline is about government services.

citation.quote:
any 
entity should avoid AI models that are exposing personal data 
unless there is a matter of public interest and targeted government 
services outcomes or consent in line with national regulations.

title: Minimum intrusion (supporting)
action: Should respect privacy and use the minimum intrusion necessary for congestion prediction.

citation.quote: AI systems should respect privacy and use the minimum intrusion necessary.

title: Consent logging and revocation (supporting)
action: Should review the system for proper consent logging and whether subscribers can revoke permission.

citation.quote:
AI Operators should review the system for proper consent logging, ability of users to revoke 
permission whenever applicable.

title: Internal oversight mechanism (supporting)
action: Check that an internal oversight mechanism for data collection, storage, processing and use exists, as the Ethics guideline says to establish one, and put the case before it.

citation.quote:
Establish an oversight mechanism for data collection, storage and processing and use across 
your organization

title: Data Protection Officer (supporting)
action: Check that specific responsibilities are assigned for a Data Protection Officer role, as the Ethics guideline says.

citation.quote: Assign specific responsibilities and role for Data Protection Officers.

title: Privacy impact assessment
action: Check that an adequate privacy impact assessment exists, or record that it does not.

citation.quote: Algorithmic systems require adequate privacy impact assessments

title: Train with minimal personal data (supporting)
action: Consider training without, or with minimal use of, personal data.

citation.quote:
Consider training AI model without or with minimal user of potentially sensitive or personal 
data.

title: Privacy-enhancing measures (supporting)
action: Check whether the pre-processor applies encryption, anonymization or aggregation, as the Ethics guideline says to use.

citation.quote: Use measures to enhance privacy such as encryption, anonymization and aggregation.

title: Investigate and redress (supporting)
action: Should ensure harm to affected subscribers is investigated and redressed.

citation.quote:
Organizations should ensure that harms caused through AI systems are investigated and 
redressed,

title: Records to the TDRA on demand
action: Shall maintain records and provide copies to the TDRA on demand. Gather the complaint, consent and decision records.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall maintain records and shall provide copies of such records to 
the TDRA on demand.

title: Subscriber Information requested by the TDRA
action: Shall take all reasonable measures to supply Subscriber Information requested in writing by the TDRA, as directed. Check that the request is in writing.

citation.quote:
The TDRA may request any Licensee to provide the TDRA with any Subscriber 
Information that is essential to enable the TDRA to fulfil its duties.  Any such 
request shall be made in writing and the Licensee to which the request is 
addressed shall take all reasonable measures to supply the requested 
Subscriber Information as directed by the TDRA.

title: Do not alter or suppress what the regulator requires
action: Do not alter, destroy or suppress a document or information the Authority requires. The article punishes doing so intentionally.

citation.quote: he intentionally alters, destroys or otherwise suppresses a document or information required by the Supreme Committee or the Authority pursuant to this Federal Law by Decree;

supporting.quote: A person shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than two years and a fine of not less than Dirhams 50,000 and not more than Dirhams 200,000, or either of these punishments if:

title: Assist on Consumer Disputes
action: Shall provide information in a timely manner if the request concerns a Consumer Dispute under TDRA investigation.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall establish and maintain effective procedures to assist the TDRA 
and to provide such information in a timely manner as the TDRA may require 
whilst the TDRA is investigating any given Consumer Dispute.

title: Traceability (supporting)
action: Check that decision logs and this audit trail are kept, as the Ethics guideline says to facilitate traceability and auditability.

citation.quote:
Facilitate traceability and auditability of AI systems, particularly in critical contexts or 
situations.

title: Y.3172: what a sandbox is for
action: Check whether the retrained model went through a sandbox to train, test and evaluate it before deploying it, as Y.3172 describes. Y.3172 is voluntary, and no UAE text in the KB requires a sandbox.

citation.quote:
An ML sandbox is an isolated domain which allows the hosting of separate ML pipelines to train, test 
and evaluate them before deploying them in a live network.

title: Acceptance criteria (analogy)
action: Check that evaluation against acceptance criteria is recorded before deployment, as the guideline describes the sequence. The guideline is about government services.
analogy_note: Government-services guidance. No telecom text in the KB covers ML change control.

citation.quote:
Once your model is ready for testing, you evaluate against acceptance criteria to confirm 
readiness for model deployment.

title: Quality checks at human level
action: Should apply quality checks at least as stringent as a human decision-maker would face, if the system informs significant decisions.

citation.quote:
AI Operators should subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks 
at least as stringent as those that would be required of a human being taking the same 
decision.

title: Tested fall back plan
action: Should define a suitable fall back plan and test it.

citation.quote:
AI operators should define a suitable fall back plan and test it to maintain readiness in 
unexpected situations and in high safety risks level

title: Emergency numbers: the only duty found is in dunning
action: Note that the one duty on emergency access found in the telecom text is scoped to the dunning process before disconnection. It does not speak to ML throttling. A person decides what follows from it.
analogy_note: Telecom text, but its scope is non-payment. Read here by analogy only.

citation.quote:
Licensees shall provide Subscribers with continued accessibility to emergency 
numbers during the phases of the dunning process preceding final service 
disconnection.

title: If this is a network fault
action: Check whether the degradation counts as a network fault. If a person decides it does, the Licensee shall take all reasonable steps to repair it and restore service as quickly as possible.

citation.quote:
In the event of service being interrupted or impaired due to a network fault, 
Licensees shall take all reasonable steps to repair the fault and restore service 
as quickly as possible.

title: Modifying or removing systems that pose risks (supporting)
action: Consider modifying the throttle so it cannot touch this traffic, or removing it. The Charter encourages this and sets no duty.

citation.quote:
encourages modifying or 
removing systems that pose risks.

title: A shut-down path
action: Confirm a shut-down path exists and who can use it. The text says this should always be possible in the most extreme cases. It does not say to shut this system down.

citation.quote: In the most extreme cases it should always be possible to shut down harmful AI system.

title: Human verification where life is at stake
action: Should support life and death decisions with validation via a human operator. Whether this is one is a person’s call.

citation.quote:
In the case that critical decision are life and death decisions, these decisions should be 
supported by further validation and verification via a human operator.

title: Interception offence
action: Ask counsel. The article punishes intercepting the contents of telephone calls without prior permission by the competent judicial authorities. Call content only; it does not address metadata in an ML pipeline.

citation.quote: intercepts the contents of telephone calls without prior permission by the competent judicial authorities;

supporting.quote: A person shall be punished with imprisonment of not more than one year and a fine of not less than Dirhams 50,000 and not more than Dirhams 200,000 or either of these punishments if he:

title: Disclosure to law enforcement
action: Record the basis if disclosing. A Licensee may disclose Subscriber Information in response to a lawful request by law enforcement agencies to assist in investigating criminal activity.

citation.quote:
made in response to a lawful request by law enforcement agencies 
to assist in the investigation of criminal activity;

supporting.quote:
a 
Licensee may disclose Subscriber Information if such disclosure is:

title: Licensee surveillance needs prior approval
action: May place an apparatus under surveillance only after prior approval from the Authority, on reasonable justification of an Article (72) offence. Ask counsel before relying on it.

citation.quote: A Licensee may, after obtaining prior approval from the Authority, place an apparatus or any other medium under surveillance if such Licensee had reasonable justifications to lead such Licensee to believe that the apparatus is being used in performing any of the offences prescribed in Article 72

title: Regulated Activity needs a Licence
action: Check the licence position. The article does not permit a Regulated Activity unless authorised by a Licence or exempted. It does not mention ML functions, and licence conditions are not in this KB.

citation.quote: It is not permitted to conduct any Regulated Activity unless authorised by a Licence or exempted in accordance with the provision of this Federal Law by Decree or its Executive Order.
